questionText: Consider a non-pipelined processor operating at $2.5\text{ GHz}$. It takes $5$ clock cycles to complete an instruction. You are going to make a $5$-stage pipeline out of this processor. Overheads associated with pipelining force you to operate the pipelined processor at $2\text{ GHz}$. In a given program, assume that $30\%$ are memory instructions, $60\%$ are ALU instructions and the rest are branch instructions. $5\%$ of the memory instructions cause stalls of $50$ clock cycles each due to cache misses and $50\%$ of the branch instructions cause stalls of $2$ cycles each. Assume that there are no stalls associated with the execution of ALU instructions. For this program, the speedup achieved by the pipelined processor over the non-pipelined processor (round off to 2 decimal places) is ________.
explanation:
Step 1: Calculate execution time per instruction for Non-Pipelined Processor
Frequency $(f_{\text{non-pipe}}) = 2.5\text{ GHz}$
Clock Cycle Time $(T_{\text{non-pipe}}) = \frac{1}{2.5\text{ GHz}} = 0.4\text{ ns}$
$\text{CPI}_{\text{non-pipe}} = 5$
Execution Time per instruction $(E_{\text{non-pipe}}) = \text{CPI}_{\text{non-pipe}} \times T_{\text{non-pipe}} = 5 \times 0.4\text{ ns} = 2.0\text{ ns}$

Step 2: Calculate average CPI and execution time for Pipelined Processor
Frequency $(f_{\text{pipe}}) = 2\text{ GHz}$
Clock Cycle Time $(T_{\text{pipe}}) = \frac{1}{2\text{ GHz}} = 0.5\text{ ns}$

Instruction Breakdown:
• Memory instructions: $30\%$, with $5\%$ causing $50$ stall cycles.
• ALU instructions: $60\%$, with $0$ stall cycles.
• Branch instructions: $100\% - (30\% + 60\%) = 10\%$, with $50\%$ causing $2$ stall cycles.

Average stall cycles per instruction:
$\text{Stalls}_{\text{avg}} = (0.30 \times 0.05 \times 50) + (0.60 \times 0) + (0.10 \times 0.50 \times 2)$
$\text{Stalls}_{\text{avg}} = 0.75 + 0 + 0.10 = 0.85\text{ cycles}$

$\text{CPI}_{\text{pipe}} = \text{Ideal CPI} + \text{Stalls}_{\text{avg}} = 1 + 0.85 = 1.85$

Execution Time per instruction $(E_{\text{pipe}}) = \text{CPI}_{\text{pipe}} \times T_{\text{pipe}} = 1.85 \times 0.5\text{ ns} = 0.925\text{ ns}$

Step 3: Calculate Speedup
$\text{Speedup} = \frac{E_{\text{non-pipe}}}{E_{\text{pipe}}} = \frac{2.0\text{ ns}}{0.925\text{ ns}} \approx 2.16216$

Rounding off to 2 decimal places gives 2.16.
